engine.description: The database the changed schema belongs to, from the driver, the SQL dialect or the migration tool; unknown when the diff does not say.

summary.description: One or two sentences in the Markdown subset: what the schema change does and the one fact a reviewer must not miss, such as a dropped column. Facts only, no advice.

migrations.description: Each place that changes the schema: a migration file, DDL embedded in code, a schema dump, an ORM model or a query file.

tables.description: Each table the pull request creates, alters, drops or renames. Empty when only queries change.

data_changes.description: Statements that change rows rather than the schema: backfills, UPDATE or DELETE in a migration, copies between tables.

text.description: What the statement does to existing rows, in one sentence.

readers.description: Code that reads or writes a changed table: queries, generated code, models. Cite it when this pull request changes it.

label.description: The function, query or file, as code names it.

updated.description: true when this pull request changes it for the new schema; false when it still uses the old one; null when unknown.

related.description: Written by the host, never by a fill: the review's risks and evidence whose code this tile cites.

hunk.description: A hunk of the diff, optionally narrowed to lines of the new file inside it.

lines.description: [first, last] line of the new file, inside the hunk's new range.

cites.description: The hunks that show it; the first is the one a reader should see.

kind.description: migration_file: a numbered or timestamped migration; embedded: DDL inside application code; schema_dump: a generated schema file; orm_model: a model that defines columns; query_file: queries only (such as sqlc).

label.description: The file name, or the function that runs the DDL.

applies.description: on_deploy: a migration tool runs it when the release deploys; on_start: the program runs it when it opens the database; manual: someone must run it.

reversible.description: true when a down migration or rollback undoes it; false when there is none or it cannot restore data; null when the tool has no such notion.

idempotent.description: true when running it twice is safe (IF NOT EXISTS, guarded ALTER); false when a second run fails or changes data again; null when the tool records what ran.

name.description: The table's name after the change, as the DDL writes it.

renamed_from.description: The old name of a renamed table; otherwise null.

columns.description: Every column of a created table; the added, removed, altered and renamed columns of any other.

indexes.description: Indexes and constraints added, removed or altered on the table: indexes, unique constraints, foreign keys, checks, triggers.

before.description: The column's definition before (type and constraints as written; for a rename, its old name first); null for an added column.

after.description: The column's definition after, as written; null for a removed column.

destructive.description: true when existing rows can lose data or start failing: a removed column, a narrowed type, NOT NULL added without a default, a rename old code still reads.

note.description: A fact the definition does not show, such as what the default fills in for existing rows; otherwise null.

name.description: The index or constraint's name; null when it has none.

definition.description: Its columns and kind, as written, such as "(repository, pr, created)" or "FOREIGN KEY (widget_id) REFERENCES widgets(id)".

online.description: Whether building it leaves the table writable: true with CONCURRENTLY or on a table this pull request creates, false for a plain build on an existing Postgres or MySQL table, null when it does not matter (SQLite) or is unknown.
